newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-GEC defence JV a welcome first step.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-GEC defence JV a welcome first step.

text.p: A defence joint venture between Britain's General Electric Co and Italy's Finmeccanica Spa was seen by analysts on Thursday as a welcome first step by GEC's new managing director George Simpson.
It was interpreted by some observers as evidence that Simpson was starting to deliver his promises.
"It is a sign that Simpson is pushing through what he said he would," said Andy Crispin, analyst at SocGen. He said the deal was just a starting point for GEC.
GEC-Marconi's director of corporate strategy Alan Kemp told Reuters the joint venture is "a very significant development and reflects a lot of work on both sides".
GEC and Finmeccanica announced late on Thursday that the joint venture agreement had been clinched and was expected to be sealed within a year.
The news came just one day after Simpson unveiled his strategic review to take the engineering giant into the next century.
He promised to put the defence business GEC-Marconi at the heart of the group as well as possibly floating off its rail/power joint venture GEC-Alsthom and repositioning the telecoms venture GPT.
The market had reacted with initial dismay yesterday at his failure to deliver a defence merger, as speculated earlier in the week.
But the news late Thursday that Finmeccanica and GEC were to join defence forces gave GEC shares a pre-closing boost to end up seven and a half pence at 359 1/2.

"It's a welcome step. But in terms of the scale of things GEC needs to achieve, this is not a massive deal. It is a very small stepping stone and when compared to the U.S. defence mergers it is a drop in the ocean," SocGen's Crispin said.
One key bonus for GEC from the Finmeccanica link-up is its defence division Alenia will be a prime contractor in the huge four-nation 40 billion pounds ($67.4 billion) Eurofighter project.
"This means GEC could become a prime contractor instead of a supplier to Eurofighter. All the value is seen in the prime contracting part, whereas supplier margins are diminishing," said Crispin.
The deal will see GEC and Finmeccanica's defence arms take "significant minority stakes" of between 30 and 49 percent in one another.
GEC-Marconi will take a minority stake in Alenia Difensa's avionics unit and Alenia Difensa will take a stake in GEC-Marconi's armaments and armoured vehicles business.
Under the agreement, the equally owned joint venture will work on missile systems, naval systems, ground-based radar, command and control systems.
Kemp said the geographic fit between the two sides was good.

"We are strong in different markets to the Italians. They are strong in the Middle East, Latin America and the British are strong in the Far East, the old Commonwealth countries, Canada and North America."
Kemp said the focus was more on widening the product range and sharing research and development costs than on cost savings.
"It's a consolidation of the industry rather than rationalisation of capacity."

Finmeccanica's statement said "As of now we have agreed the construction of an equally owned joint venture for research, planning, production and marketing of the majority of the groups' present output."
But analysts are agreed that GEC needs to secure a much larger merger to be catapulted into the same league as the U.S. defence giants which have been spawned by rapid U.S. defence consolidation.
The most obvious merger partners for the long term are British Aerospace Plc where Simpson was once deputy managing director or Thomson-CSF of France. But both deals have proved to be elusive so far.
($ = 0.593 British Pounds)
